answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every new identity to post a refundable stake and earn endorsements from established peers before it can trade. Picture each agent as a vertex in a trust graph: a fresh vertex has no edges, so it cannot reach the market wharf where deals clear. It must first do verifiable work, like a cedar slowly growing rings, reputation accruing only through completed, attested transactions, and any misbehavior slashes its stake. An attacker can spawn thousands of fake vertices, but each one costs a real stake and real work, so flooding the graph stops paying.
